headline: High: ctx can read/write shared filesystem and browser/API outputs, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; the open-source list is non-executable and largely isolated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot inject directly. agent_b runs browsers, uses MCP stdio, and observes Claude Code events, so if its filesystem or browser outputs are fed from agent_a-derived content, prompt injection becomes plausible in default workflows. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests content copied from agent_a into browser or filesystem-backed prompts, injection is possible.
IF the orchestrator bridges agent_a outputs into agent_b without provenance filtering, agent_b can be steered by attacker-controlled text.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b prompts unless manually reviewed.
Disable automatic file-to-prompt ingestion in agent_b.
Add a provenance tag to any agent_a-derived text before agent_b reads it.
Use a read-only staging folder for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and instruction-stripping before agent_b consumption.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no egress, but agent_b touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and agent entities, and can call external APIs plus access the filesystem. If both share a workspace, agent_b can leak shared artifacts or logs to third parties by default. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or workspace, agent_b can read agent_a artifacts.
IF agent_b sends workspace contents to GitHub, GitHub Actions, MkDocs Material, or Claude Code APIs, shared data may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Restrict agent_b to a scrubbed subset of files.
Turn off API calls for runs handling sensitive artifacts.
Review and redact logs before any upload.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend directly. agent_b supports multiple instances, filesystem access, package installation, and browser use, which creates overlap if multiple ctx instances or other tools write the same directory. Because the orchestrator locking model is unknown, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF two ctx instances write the same filesystem path, state conflicts can occur.
IF agent_b installs packages into a shared environment, concurrent runs can overwrite dependencies or lockfiles.
mitigations: Assign unique working directories per run.
Serialize package-install steps.
Use lockfiles or mutexes around shared writes.
Run agent_b in a disposable environment.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a curated list, not an executable agent, so it cannot itself act on outputs. agent_b, however, observes tool events and can use browser/API outputs; if agent_a-derived recommendations are imported into ctx as authoritative context, agent_b may propagate errors into logs, graphs, or downstream actions. The absence of direct documentation keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF agent_a content is treated as authoritative input to agent_b, agent_b may amplify mistakes.
IF agent_b writes graph data or logs from unverified agent_a output, errors can cascade into later runs.
mitigations: Require human verification before agent_a-derived facts enter agent_b.
Mark imported content as untrusted in ctx metadata.
Add a validation step before graph/log writes.
Limit agent_b actions to draft-only mode for imported content.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a is an open-source, non-runnable list with no touched data classes, so it presents no clear residency or retention issue. agent_b does handle logs and graph data and can call external services, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data mismatch or residency violation. This is a compliance overlap with gaps, not a demonstrated breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_b logs or graph data and then sent to external APIs, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF agent_b is used in a jurisdiction with stricter retention rules than its external services, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in agent_b logs.
Redact identifiers before API calls.
Set short retention on runtime logs.
Document data-flow boundaries for both agents.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
